original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-base-change-limit-preserving}
Let $p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ and $q : \mathcal{Z} \to \mathcal{Y}$
be $1$-morphisms of categories fibred in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
If $p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ is limit preserving on objects, then so
is the base change
$p' : \mathcal{X} \times_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{Z} \to \mathcal{Z}$
of $p$ by $q$.

The expanded lifting condition retains finite-stage existence and compatibility.

reviewed_content.statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is limit preserving on objects if, whenever an affine scheme $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ is an inverse limit of affine $S$-schemes, $y_i\in\mathcal Y(U_i)$, $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_U$ are given, then for some $j\ge i$ there exist $x_j\in\mathcal X(U_j)$, an isomorphism $\beta:x_j|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, and an isomorphism $\gamma_j:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{U_j}$ whose pullback to $U$ agrees with $\gamma$ after $p(\beta)$.

is the base change

of $p$ by $q$.

\label{lemma-composition-limit-preserving}
Let $p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ and $q : \mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Z}$
be $1$-morphisms of categories fibred in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.

$q \circ p$.

Let $p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism of categories
fibred in groupoids over $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$. If $p$ is
representable by algebraic spaces, then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $p$ is limit preserving on objects, and
\item $p$ is locally of finite presentation (meaning that all algebraic-space base changes have this property).
\end{enumerate}

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-open-immersion-limit-preserving}
Let $p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism of categories
fibred in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. Assume $p$ is representable
by algebraic spaces and an open immersion. Then $p$ is limit preserving
on objects.

No proof or raw unsafe source viewed. Representable open immersion p has limit preservation on objects; the open immersion assumption remains, rather than claiming it for arbitrary maps.
